### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bbfccbdc7842e3de6e837041194610a976cc434b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0c671722019786415289e0d4d4e83fb381a1dcd6` — the merge of head `f7ee536e2c9ba3ede0a0e27accd8070d9c144a6f` into base `bbfccbdc7842e3de6e837041194610a976cc434b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0c671722019786415289e0d4d4e83fb381a1dcd6 && git checkout 0c671722019786415289e0d4d4e83fb381a1dcd6
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin bbfccbdc7842e3de6e837041194610a976cc434b f7ee536e2c9ba3ede0a0e27accd8070d9c144a6f && git checkout -B drift-repro bbfccbdc7842e3de6e837041194610a976cc434b && git merge --no-ff f7ee536e2c9ba3ede0a0e27accd8070d9c144a6f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bbfccbdc7842e3de6e837041194610a976cc434b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs bbfccbdc7842e3de6e837041194610a976cc434b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `f7ee536e2c9ba3ede0a0e27accd8070d9c144a6f`
Local-runs: none

Read: card #29279 (body; triage 6575742201; claims 6576292695 and 6576364650; dev report 6577418310, with 6577428649 ignored as its duplicate), PR #29350 (body, 5 files, net diff against merge-base `504ba510`), and the head's check-runs. Rendered 2026-11-02T13:04Z.

Gates (check-runs on this head): all 48 completed: 35 success, 13 skipped (opt-in or path-filtered: UI build, lint, test and type-check, Docs, Dogfood matrix/CLI, upgrade harness, tarball smoke, Temporal conformance, schedule gate), 0 failure, 0 in progress. Green: Build Core, Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Type Check (workspace, consumer gates, source gates, debt ledger), Lint (ESLint, repo, PM dispatch-gates, docs and code guards, CI/release/engine, scoped), Check Changeset, Check PR Size, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Dogfood Regression Gate, Live E2E UI.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The `writeSource !== 'migrate-stored'` carve-out on the #28990 block in `saveMetaItem`: right.** It removes one refusal for one write source and adds none. `writeSource` is `request.source ?? 'protocol.saveMetaItem'`, and the server is the only party that sets it. The only producer of `'migrate-stored'` is `migrateStoredMetadata`'s own `saveMetaItem` call. The REST save door (`runtime/src/domains/meta.ts`) builds the request field by field: `metaSaveRequestOptions` (`rest/src/meta-save-request.ts`) has no `source`. `protocol.zod.ts` documents `source` as off the contract. The other in-process callers (`organization-ownership.ts`, `packages.ts`, `permission-set-clone.ts`, `automation.ts`) pass no `source`. The carve-out has the same shape as the #28952 seed rule and the ADR-0138 D2b elevated-flow rule beside it. Ablation A2 in the PR body (widened to every draft, 3 failed) shows the PR does not admit an author's draft save.
   **What it admits beyond the card's literal case.** Two things, both bounded to bodies already at rest:
   (a) A pass re-save of a draft that has an active row, where the draft grants on a gone object that the active row does not hold. It was `failed` and is now `rewritten`. This is the same class as the card's case: a pre-rule draft at rest, still judged at its publish by the unchanged `promoteDraftForPublish` call.
   (b) A pass re-save of an active row. This is not observable, because the held keys were already read from that same row.
   The pass cannot add a new grant key. It writes only the converted body of the row it read. None of the permission conversions in the ledger (`managedBy`, `allowRestore`/`allowPurge`, RLS `tags`) renames an `objects` key. So no grant name reaches the store that was not already there. Nothing an author or client can claim is widened.
2. **The publish-path refusal wording: right, and prose only.** The `door: 'save' | 'publish'` parameter defaults to `'save'`. Only `promoteDraftForPublish` passes `'publish'`, which covers `publishMetaItem` and `publishPackageDrafts`. The save door and the restore doors (`protocol-authoring-gate.ts` passes 3 args) keep "…and none is saved here…". On the publish path the text after "which is not defined in objects: " becomes "no package registers an object of that name, and no published object, or object draft of this batch, carries it". That is the card's dictated sentence, and it reaches `err.message` through `specValidationFindings` too.
   Nothing a client can branch on moves: `code: INVALID_METADATA`, `status: 422`, issue `code: 'custom'`, the path `objects.NAME`, the issue count and order, and the leading "Permission 'SET' grants on object 'NAME' which is not defined in objects" are all unchanged. A repo-wide grep at this head finds no consumer keyed on "none is saved here" other than the unit test this PR updates. The dogfood pin, the restore-door family test, `defineStack` and Studio key on the leading sentence.
   Nit, non-blocking: on a single-item `publishMetaItem` there is no batch (`pending` is undefined), so "object draft of this batch" names a batch that does not exist. The sentence is still true there.
3. **Signature change: internal only.** The extra trailing optional parameter is on a `private` method and on a function in `protocol-save-door-refusals.ts`. The package's single `.` export (`index.ts`) does not re-export that file, so the published TS surface does not change.
4. **Forced test edits: right.** Three publish-path assertions now expect the publish wording. The `publishPackageDrafts` case moves from the `grants on object` fragment to the whole first sentence, which is stronger. The new `[#29279]` unit describe and the real-kernel objectql file pin the measured case (`rewritten`, key stripped, grant kept, still a draft), its publish refused at `objects.qa_widget`, the control with the object draft present, and an author re-save still refused. Clearing the planted row's `checksum` keeps the premise honest (`storedBodyUnchanged`), as the PR explains.
5. Nit, non-blocking: the held-check comment in `protocol-save-door-refusals.ts` still lists "a stored-row migration" as a write the held check serves. No `migrate-stored` write reaches that check now. The `protocol.ts` docblock was corrected; this comment is stale but harmless.

No must-fix.

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset `.changeset/29279-migrate-stored-draft-permission-grant.md`: `'@objectstack/metadata-protocol': patch`. It matches what the diff publishes.** The source change is in `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` only. The objectql file is a test, so objectql needs no entry. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: no key, value, type or default that an author can write changes. Under AGENTS.md, `none` takes `patch`. `skip-changeset` would be wrong (a released package's behaviour moves) and is not used. Check Changeset passed on this head.
- **Clause-②: yes (widening). The PR body and the changeset both declare it, and it is correct.** A public entry, `os migrate meta --stored --apply` / `POST /api/v1/meta/_migrate-stored`, now reports a row `rewritten` where `main` reported `failed` (422).
  Nothing accepted on `main` is refused at this head:
  - the only gate edit removes a refusal for one source;
  - the `door` parameter changes message prose and adds no throw;
  - every other door's inputs and order are unchanged.
  So there is no `(narrowing)` arm and no `!`.
  The card's own "Level" note says `Clause-②: no`. That is superseded by the seat claim's `yes (widening)` and by the measured outcome change. `no` would understate a changed outcome on a public entry.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **open_questions[0]: keep the "refused at its publish" line in the 29279 changeset, or also amend the pending 28990 one? Answer: A, keep it in the 29279 changeset. Do not amend `28990-permission-grant-unknown-object.md`.**
  - The 28990 changeset is not false without the line. Its "Where" bullet already names the publish of a draft (`POST /meta/permission/NAME/publish`, `publish-drafts`) as a refusing door. Its quoted finding ends in "…", so the new publish wording does not contradict it.
  - Its "What is not judged" bullet says `os migrate meta --stored` is not refused. That was untrue for the draft-only row class, and this PR is what makes it true.
  - Both changesets are pending and ship in the same release.
  - Editing a pending changeset would red `check-empty-changeset` and need a declared deliberate correction, for no reader gain.
- **Card file-surface bounds (claim 6576364650): all held.** No `packages/spec/**`. No new error code. No change to the refusal on a user save: the save wording is byte-identical, and the carve-out is keyed on server-stated provenance.
- **Card fix items 1–3: all delivered.**
  - Item 1 chose the #28952-style carve-out over reading held keys from the draft row. The rationale is sound: reading the draft would also have widened an author's draft re-save, which the card rules out.
  - Item 2: the wording is verbatim the card's.
  - Item 3: the changeset's "Now" bullet carries the line, following the `26724-object-unknown-datasource-refused.md` precedent.
- **Dev deviations: accepted.**
  - Skipping the PR assign/review-request step is right: os-dev forbids assignees and MCP writes.
  - ESLint on the touched files is acceptable, since neither package has a `lint` script. CI's `Lint · ESLint` is green on this head.
  - The checksum clearing in the premise test is explained above.
- **security_findings `none` and out_of_scope_findings `[]`: no escalation owed.**

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-vqzr9r`
Reviewed-by: `session_01ADHkmQjPiXgNoSaEpqeGvY`

**VERDICT: PASS**
